result.proposed_fix: Build _STROKES in canonical form: frozenset(normalise(ch) for ch in <listed chars> + Kangxi U+2F00-U+2FD5 + CJK Radicals Supplement U+2E80-U+2EF3), keeping only single-letter results (and the 'ᆞ' NFKC target of 'ㆍ'). Explicitly add the unified single- and few-stroke radicals 一 U+4E00, 丨 U+4E28, 乙 U+4E59, 亅 U+4E85, 乚, 二 U+4E8C, 亠 U+4EA0. Drop the non-letter U+31C0 range (it already acts as non-letter gap). Add a module-level assertion or test that every member satisfies normalise(c)==c and _letter(c). Add a self-contained regression test that checks every 2-letter combination of the stroke set (incl. Kangxi spellings) through has_link_or_contact, mask_links, SY.verify, SY.extractive, build_surface + require_valid, with controls '中国' (owner-accepted residual) and 'Tokyo 東京 is big' (must stay readable).
result.root_cause: The D17 'stroke and dot-shaped letters' allow-list _STROKES (uri_web/untrusted.py:516-517) is built from raw code points that never occur in the text it is checked against. normalise() applies NFKC first (untrusted.py:255), which maps every Kangxi radical U+2F00-U+2FD5 to its unified ideograph (U+2F00->U+4E00, U+2F01->U+4E28, ...). So the Kangxi range in _STROKES can never match: all 214 code points are NFKC-unstable and 211 of their normalised forms are absent from the set. The CJK Strokes range U+31C0-U+31E3 is category So, not a letter, so it never forms part of a word either. Only about 11 entries can match (丶丿乀乁乚亅ᆞᆢ・･〆〇), and the basic single-stroke radicals 一 U+4E00, 丨 U+4E28, 乙 U+4E59 (and 二, 亠, ...) are missing. _separator_word (line 549: len(letters)==1 or letters <= _STROKES) therefore returns False for '丨丶', '一丶', '丶一', '乙丶', '⼁⼂', '⼀⼂'. The walk at line 562 stops there and takes the word as the name; the gap is plain prose and 'shop' is not core, so the match is dropped at line 573, and the link passes has_link_or_contact, mask_links, verify, extractive, the surface and the A2UI validator.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: Repairs 1-7 (ca622bc0..7b1252f7) date from rounds R1-R9 and never touch _separator_word or _STROKES. The R13 repairs were coordinator commits. 842ad64d used the rule 'foreign word with <= _MAX_FOREIGN (2) distinct letters is a separator', which would have caught '丨丶'. da10d0b8 (owner loosening) replaced it with the _STROKES allow-list, written as raw Unicode block ranges without accounting for the NFKC/letter-category canonicalisation applied by normalise()/_words(). Its regression test (tests/web/test_w1_closure_r13_review_regressions.py LINKS) only replays the reviewer's literal strings (丶丿, ㆍᆢ, ʘʘ, ǃǃ), whose characters happen to be among the ~11 live members, so the 31 tests pass while the class stays open. The same pattern as R11->R12->R13: each patch matched the reviewer's specific strings instead of the rule.
